introduction: This intermediate tier explores the massive legislative replacements of 2025. It details the end of MGNREGA, the repeal of the 60-year-old Income Tax Act, modern immigration controls, and the controversial restructuring of the Election Commission.

core_concepts.title: Viksit Bharat—G RAM G Act, 2025 (Replacing MGNREGA)
core_concepts.description:
The Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025 completely repeals and replaces the MGNREGA (2005).
- Key Changes: Increases guaranteed employment from 100 to **125 days** per rural household. 
- Funding Shift: Alters the funding ratio to a **60:40** (Centre:State) split. 
- Technology & Climate: Mandates biometric authentication and geo-mapping of assets, shifting the focus from short-term wage support to creating climate-resilient, durable rural infrastructure.

core_concepts.title: The Income Tax Act, 2025
core_concepts.description:
Passed in late 2025 (effective April 1, 2026), this act repeals the six-decade-old Income Tax Act of 1961.
- Objective: Consolidates, restructures, and massively simplifies the highly patched 1961 code. It aims to reduce interpretational litigation, streamline tax brackets, and foster a more taxpayer-friendly, digitized assessment regime.

core_concepts.title: Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025
core_concepts.description:
Repealed four outdated colonial/pre-2000 laws, including the Foreigners Act of 1946.
- Mandates: Introduces strict mandatory reporting for hotels, hospitals, and universities hosting foreign nationals. 
- Statutory Status: For the first time, it provides independent statutory backing to the **Bureau of Immigration**, authorizing it to independently identify, detain, and deport illegal foreigners.

core_concepts.title: Chief Election Commissioner and Other ECs Act, 2023
core_concepts.description:
A highly debated law that reversed the Supreme Court's ruling in the *Anoop Baranwal* case.
- The Change: The Supreme Court had mandated that the Election Commission be appointed by a panel comprising the PM, Leader of Opposition (LoP), and the Chief Justice of India (CJI). 
- The Act: Parliament passed this law replacing the CJI with a **Union Cabinet Minister** nominated by the PM, thereby giving the Executive a 2:1 majority in selecting the independent Election Commissioners.

important_entities.name: Repealing and Amending Act, 2025
important_entities.key_fact: Scrapped 71 obsolete laws from the statute books.
important_entities.significance: A major 'legislative housekeeping' effort to improve the ease of governance. It notably removed Section 213 of the Indian Succession Act, eliminating community-based disparities in probate requirements, ensuring uniform fairness in succession.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If a current affairs question asks about rural employment guarantees in 2026, do NOT select MGNREGA. It has been formally replaced by the **Viksit Bharat – G RAM G Act, 2025**, which changed the guarantee to 125 days and altered the funding matrix.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember that the 2023 Act specifically removed the Chief Justice of India from the selection committee to assert parliamentary sovereignty over appointments.

exam_strategy_tips: In UPSC Mains, when discussing border security or demographic challenges, heavily cite the **Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025** as the modern legal framework granting statutory teeth to the Bureau of Immigration.
